about.title: About Me
about.homelab.title: Homelab & Self-Hosting
about.homelab.text: My homelab lives on an old laptop running CasaOS, feeding my family and me: file and image storage, adblock and streaming services. I hide access behind an nginx reverse proxy and use Headscale to build a private network, so everyone can connect from anywhere. It gave me plenty of headaches, but I learned more running it than in any course — and it made me the family hero whenever a movie needs playing.
about.linux.title: Linux & Ricing
about.linux.text: Linux is my daily driver as a developer. Since I'm not always the only one using the machine, I had to create and manage separate users: some get the basics, others get restricted permissions so a bad move can't break the system. I also built shortcuts that hide the complexity from my family, who aren't exactly tech-savvy. I left fragile distros like Arch behind and switched to Fedora, which gives me a stable environment without giving up new features. And yes, I like to tweak down to the very last detail so everything looks the way I want — that brought its share of frustrations and more than one broken system, but I learned a ton about how Linux actually works. You can check the result in my dotfiles.
about.ai.title: Dev Setup: Tools & AI Agents
about.ai.text: I don't have rigid workflows; I just tune my editors to how I work. Right now that's Neovim and Zed, kept as minimal and efficient as possible. Since I don't pay for AI providers, I set up Opencode with a model rotator that switches providers in a balanced way so I never run out of tokens. I keep a simple config, with custom skills that automate my repetitive tasks and processes.
about.background.title: Student & Developer
about.background.text: I studied Computer Systems Analysis at FAMAF-UNC. I lean toward backend and infrastructure because my frontend tastes shift constantly and design has cost me more than a few headaches (this portfolio got a fresh look about five times), while backend feels like playing with LEGO: everything clicks into place satisfyingly when you do it right. On the infrastructure side I love automating processes, working with hardware, and squeezing every drop out of whatever resources I have at hand. In a world that increasingly trades optimization for raw compute and speed, making do with little forces you to weigh strengths against weaknesses and to prioritize instead of doing everything at once.
project.desc.switcher: Web game featuring real-time bidirectional communication and constant synchronization across multiple clients. It implements session persistence to ensure match recovery during unexpected disconnections. The system includes a chronological flow control engine, enabling state reversibility for move-by-move undo functionality.
project.desc.omnet: Project focused on analyzing simulated network environments using communication protocols. Leveraging OMNeT++ to model interconnected nodes, the study evaluated flow control and congestion issues through performance metrics. A dynamic rate-adaptation algorithm was developed to respond to network congestion, effectively minimizing packet loss and optimizing data throughput.
project.desc.dsl: A domain-specific language for creating and transforming complex geometric figures. It leverages vector-based semantics for rotations and overlays, featuring an interactive mode with Gloss to design patterns and Escher-style tilings in real-time.
project.desc.parser: A massive data processing system designed to automate content extraction from multiple web subscriptions and forums. The engine transforms heterogeneous sources into a Resilient Distributed Dataset (RDD/DataFrame), orchestrating a network of Workers to apply filtering heuristics and entity extraction in parallel. The result is a structured data feed that achieves efficient synthesis of scattered information into a unified format.
project.desc.gogym: Full-stack application to record your progress in the gym with a high level of detail. Designed to calculate effective volume, effort (RIR) and mechanical resistance profiles.
project.desc.spicetify: An extension made for Spicetify that allows to link together songs in a playlist that should reproduce one after the other in shuffle mode.
